title: BetNowly: Building a Social Betting Ledger

blocks.text: BetNowly is a social betting ledger for creating, sharing, tracking, and settling informal bets. It gives participants a trusted record of the terms, roles, evidence, and final outcome—without managing payments. Friend groups are the initial use case, alongside couples, fantasy leagues, gaming communities, and other social groups.

Andy defined a social betting ledger category, removed participation friction, corrected a trust-breaking product-model issue based on beta behavior, and instrumented the funnel required to validate growth.
The Product Loop
Decision One: Remove Participation Friction

The primary drop-off risk was the invite wall. If an invited participant had to create an account before accepting a bet, most wouldn't. I allowed users to engage with a shared bet link before creating an account, then claim their participation history afterward. This reduced the setup required before the social interaction could begin.

items.title: Shareable Links
items.description: Each bet generates a unique link shareable in any messaging app—no install required to view or accept.

items.title: Guest Participation
items.description: Invited participants can accept and interact with a bet before creating an account, keeping the social moment intact.

items.title: Account Claiming
items.description: Guests can later create an account and claim their full bet history—nothing is lost from anonymous participation.

blocks.text: Additional capabilities include friends autocomplete, one-tap bet templates, and cross-device ticket history.
Decision Two: Fix a Trust-Breaking Product-Model Issue

Beta users were entering verification instructions—"check ESPN" or "whoever scored more wins"—into the Judge field. This revealed a mismatch between the interface and the underlying concept. Judges decide outcomes; proof methods verify them. Conflating the two created ambiguity about who was responsible for settling a bet and how.

blocks.title: Judge vs. Proof: Before and After
before: Judge field accepted people or verification instructions
Existing malformed tickets could become stuck
Constraints depended too heavily on the interface
after: Judge is restricted to a real participant
Admin repair tooling corrects affected records
Client- and server-side validation enforce integrity

blocks.text: The fix separated Judge—the person responsible for deciding the outcome—from Proof—the method used to verify the result. Each bet moves through defined states (active, pending settlement, settled, disputed, reconsidered, voided), making every transition intentional and auditable. Dual-layer validation enforces role constraints in the UI and again server-side to prevent bypass.

items.title: Judge and Proof Separated
items.description: Made settlement ownership explicit and prevented non-person values from being assigned as judges.

items.title: One Role Per Identity
items.description: A participant cannot hold conflicting roles on the same bet—enforced at both the client and server level.

items.title: Audited Resolution
items.description: Disputed outcomes can be reviewed and resolved by an admin with a full audit trail, giving participants a meaningful escalation path.

blocks.text: Decision Three: Instrument the Funnel

Rather than tracking aggregate traffic, I instrumented the full acquisition and participation funnel so future prioritization could be based on where users actually abandoned the loop—not where I assumed they did.

Each transition maps to a specific friction point: created → shared identifies sharing friction; invited → accepted identifies invitation friction; accepted → settled identifies completion friction; settled → repeat creation measures retention.

items.title: Acquisition Funnel
items.description: Every step from landing to bet creation to first invite is tracked, including time-to-action measurements that surface where momentum stalls.

items.title: Referral Attribution
items.description: Tracks which bets and users generated new sign-ups, enabling referral loop analysis rather than just top-line user counts.

items.title: Needs Attention Queue
items.description: An operational view of bets stuck in ambiguous states—overdue settlements, unresolved disputes—so issues surface before users notice them.

blocks.text: SEO-to-bet-creation tracking connects organic search arrivals to downstream bet creation, measuring whether intent-specific landing pages drive actual product engagement.
Technical Execution

Built with Claude Code, vanilla JavaScript, Vercel serverless functions, and Neon Postgres. I implemented custom funnel instrumentation, validation tooling, and a data-driven landing-page generator to support rapid iteration without adding framework or analytics dependencies.
Current Evidence
Launched a functional end-to-end bet lifecycle: create, share, accept, settle, dispute, and void.
Instrumented acquisition through settlement with explicit drop-off tracking.
Revised the Judge/Proof model based on observed beta behavior.
Published nine intent-specific landing pages connected to bet creation tracking.
Implemented referral attribution and guest-to-account claiming.
Next Validation Milestone
Determine whether invited groups complete and repeat bets without founder prompting, measured through invitation acceptance, settlement rate, and 30-day repeat creation.
